intro: I build enterprise applications on the Microsoft Power Platform for New York State agencies, and I am a certified Power Platform developer. My work turns manual, spreadsheet-based, and legacy processes into secure, maintainable applications that people can rely on.
background: I studied Mathematics Education in Ghana, Statistics at Rutgers University, and Biostatistics at the New Jersey Institute of Technology. That training shapes how I approach data models, analysis, and reporting: I want the data to be structured correctly before anyone builds on it.
interests: Dataverse data modeling, model-driven apps, Power Automate, and the security and lifecycle practices that keep solutions safe to run in production. I also work with SQL, Python, R, Power BI, and GIS data collection with ArcGIS Survey123.
journey: After operations and analysis work at Amazon, I moved into public-sector technology at the New York Department of State in 2023. There I built the Fiscal Contract Manager and led several migrations from SharePoint, InfoPath, and Oracle onto the Power Platform. In 2026 I joined the New York State Office of Information Technology Services and also advised on Power Platform architecture and security for an AI platform on a short contract.
philosophy: To become a solution architect and technical leader, building innovative technology solutions that drive digital transformation and solve complex business problems. I believe in using technology, continuous learning, and collaboration to create secure, practical, and sustainable solutions that deliver meaningful impact.
learning: Exploring AI-enabled solutions on the Power Platform, including Code Apps and AI Builder, and how governance, security, and ALM practices apply to them.
